title: Hollywood takes on Zuckerberg, Musk and Altman amid widespread anxiety over AI
source_used: The News International (account of the CNBC story); CNET (background, 9 Oct 2026)
key_facts: Hollywood is releasing films about tech leaders Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Sam Altman as public concern about AI grows (The News International's account of the CNBC story).

The films named: Aaron Sorkin's “The Social Reckoning” (Zuckerberg and Meta), Alex Gibney's nearly four-hour documentary “Musk”, and “Artificial” from Neon, a scripted film about Altman due at Christmas.
Musk has criticised the Gibney documentary on X, saying it has zero integrity.
Altman told CNBC: “I get why people have anxiety” and that being teased “doesn’t bother” him.
The public has grown more apprehensive about AI and wary of the data centers that power it.
The account compares the trend with films that shifted opinion before, such as “The Day After Tomorrow” and “Blackfish”.

CNET (9 Oct 2026) independently lists the same three films; it says “The Social Reckoning” draws on leaked papers from Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen and that “Musk” opens in theaters on 16 Oct.
quote_evidence: Hollywood is shifting its focus toward technology leaders such as Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Sam Altman as concerns about artificial intelligence continue to grow.
These films have come at a turning point as the public has grown increasingly apprehensive regarding the perils of AI and wary of the data centers that power the technology.
Hollywood is unleashing a handful of movies this fall, pulling the curtain back to shine a light on some of the big names in tech
why_it_matters_hint: Films about AI-era tech leaders are reaching audiences while public worry about AI grows.
event_date: 10 Oct 2026 (CNBC story); films released from October to Christmas 2026
notes: CNBC page returned 403 (blocked). Text read from The News International, which rewrites the CNBC story (it quotes Altman ‘in conversation with CNBC’); film details cross-checked in CNET. The News International text is loose in places and says the Musk film opens ‘this weekend’, while CNET says 16 Oct; the entry avoids release dates except Christmas for ‘Artificial’.
